catalog_quote: Selon les données de P. Medjo Mvé et Y. Nzang Bie (2023), le système tonal du mwesa est constitué de trois registres de base: le tonème haut (H), le tonème bas (B) et le tonème moyen (M). Ce dernier n'est observé qu'avec des thèmes de structures CV. On relève également deux tons modulés: le ton montant et le ton descendant, qui sont considérés comme rares comparés aux tons ponctuels, du moins au niveau du lexique.

new_statements.translation: According to the data of P. Medjo Mvé and Y. Nzang Bie (2023), the tone system of Mwesa consists of three basic registers: the high toneme (H), the low toneme (B) and the mid toneme (M). The latter is observed only with stems of CV structure. Two contour tones are also noted, rising and falling, which are considered rare compared with level tones, at least at the lexical level.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Mwesa is described as a register-tone language (H, L, and a marginal M restricted to CV stems, plus rare rising/falling contours) with lexically distinctive tone; no word stress or accent is described anywhere in the accessible literature. The only accent-related remark is a group-level (B20) diachronic speculation that loss of H tone on stem-final syllables may point toward an accentual development (Koumbi Mabiti 2025: 237, citing Rekanga 2007 and Dodo-Bouguendza 2010).
new_statements.exceptions: Mid tone only on CV stems; contour tones rare at the lexical level. Group-level: H/L opposition 'tend à disparaître en T2' (second stem syllable) across B20 parlers, with Mwesa among those not showing *BB > HB (p. 237).
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical/stem level ('au niveau du lexique'); statement is a summary of Medjo Mvé & Nzang Bie 2023's synchronic phonology, embedded in a comparative-diachronic dissertation; no phrase-level or citation-form discussion.
new_statements.identity_note: Mwesa = Mesa = Yesa (Mouloungui 1999 'mesa'); Maho 2009 NUGL code B22E (Kele group, Bantu B20); Koumbi Mabiti 2025 reclassify it 'B26B' in his own revised B20 scheme. Spoken only in the village Imbong (Djouah canton, Zadié department, Ogooué-Ivindo, ~7 km NE of Mékambo) by 100-150 speakers (Medjo Mvé & Nzang Bie 2023: 13, via Koumbi Mabiti 2025: 115-116). No ISO code; Glottolog mwes1234.

sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent for Mwesa. Mwesa section I.2.3.5 (pp. 115-118) summarises Medjo Mvé & Nzang Bie 2023: 7 vowels, 16 consonants, tone system of three basic registers H, B (low), M (M only on CV stems) plus rare rising and falling contours 'au niveau du lexique' (§I.2.3.5.3, p. 118). Group-level diachronic remark (p. 237): H tone is being lost in stem-final position (T2) across B20, which 'pourrait conforter, comme l'ont suggéré Rekanga (2007, p. 26) et Dodo-Bouguendza (2010, p. 78), une évolution vers un processus accentuel' — a speculation about the B20 group, not a stress rule.
